correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivative tests give the three displayed conditional expectations. Each conditional residual is exactly a coordinate speed divided by its coefficient, so conditional orthogonality yields the three variance decompositions and the three covariance identities. For the first defect, zero mean-square x-speed forces x constant on compact invariant support, then y=-x, then x(1-kz)=0; compactness and d>0 rule out x=0, giving z=1/k and x^2=d/g, exactly the two equilibria. Conversely, any measure supported on those equilibria has zero first defect. The strict variance and correlation statements follow immediately. The packaged exact checker independently verifies the residual and variance/covariance algebra and the equilibrium equations.

value.rationale: The Burke–Shaw flow couples a linear relaxation pair to a quadratic feedback channel, and prior work already shows that its bounded recurrent regimes obey nontrivial global forcing balances. The accepted result resolves those balances fiber by fiber: it identifies the exact conditional predictor for each coupled input and interprets the unexplained residual as coordinate-speed energy. This produces universal covariance signs, an exact orthogonality law for the forcing product \(xy\) against the height \(z\), and a complete equilibrium equality case for the x–y variance gap. These are directly testable consistency conditions for periodic or bounded chaotic invariant states and are structurally stronger than scalar time averages.
